metadata.title: Isabelle/HOL formal development for "A Theoretical Study of DBLog"
metadata.description:
Machine-checked Isabelle/HOL formal development accompanying the paper "A Theoretical Study of DBLog: Certified Virtual Cuts for a Snapshot-Equivalent Replay of Live Databases" by Andreas Andreakis.

DBLog is studied as a snapshot-equivalent replay protocol for live databases: it produces a logical, replay-equivalent snapshot of a live database scope without taking a physical database snapshot. The central formal object is the certified virtual cut — a finite, asynchronously gathered mix of change-data-capture events and chunk reads whose certified replay reaches the same state as the source at a chosen frontier on a chosen key scope.

The session DBLog_Virtual_Cuts comprises 38 theory files, builds sorry-free under Isabelle2025-2 using HOL-Library only, and generates its own entry document (PDF). The development is conservative throughout: it declares no axioms, every witness and counterexample fixture is a constructed instance, and the only type not introduced as a datatype or record is a conservative typedef for source coordinates. A public checker model exhibits all nine headline theorems non-degenerately on a constructed witness. The kernel checks the proofs under the conditional premises stated in each theorem; it does not, and cannot, discharge the deployment obligations or the external-observation assumption that a real deployment must establish. See README.md inside the archive for build instructions and a description of the main results.

Version 2.1 repairs a defect found by an external review of the 2.0 artifact: the same-evidence negative control in the Layer 3 fixtures failed to materialize its run, so the accessor-agreement comparison it advertises was never exercised (a vacuous control; no theorem statement was affected). The repair makes the control materialize, and a new kernel-checked regression theory pins that reachability. The nine headline theorem statements are unchanged from 2.0; the repaired control's own statement is strictly strengthened.

Version 2.0 rebuilds the development's foundations in this conservative, axiom-free style — version 1.0 introduced its witnesses and counterexample fixtures by axiomatization. The theorem statements are unchanged.
